You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.output:
For recurring task-d4c70c99, the grid has two equal-sized panels separated by a single uniform divider (vertical or horizontal). Find the color value occurring in both panels; output a panel-sized grid filled with that shared color, and put 3 wherever both corresponding cells have the shared color. Otherwise leave the shared-color background. Evidence: demos had shared 9 in pairs 1–2, shared 5 in pair 3, and shared 6 in pair 4. A solved test used shared 7 and output 12x13, with 3 at aligned 7/7 cells. Another solved test was 10x25 with vertical divider 4 at column 13 (1-based), panels 10x12, shared color 0; output had 3 at 1-based positions (2,4), (3,8), (4,3), (4,9), (4,11), (5,1), (5,2), (5,6), (5,8), (5,10), (6,2), (9,6), (10,12), and 0 elsewhere. Critical: parse each row into exact widths and compare same relative coordinates. A wrong first attempt came from manually misreading right-panel zero positions in rows 3 and 8; splitting at the divider and calculating programmatically avoided this.

Additional confirmed test (task-d4c70c99): 25x18 grid split horizontally into two 12x18 panels by a full row of color 1. Top panel colors {2,9}, bottom panel {0,9}, so shared color is 9. The sole top-panel 9 at zero-based (9,1) does not align with any bottom-panel 9; output is a 12x18 grid entirely filled with 9 (no 3 cells). This confirms empty overlap is still a valid uniform output.

Additional confirmed test: 8x27 grid with vertical divider color 7 at column 14 (1-based), two 8x13 panels. Their sole shared palette color was 6. Output was 8x13 filled with 6, with a single 3 at zero-based (7,11) where the aligned cells were both 6. Confirms the rule with a dense 6/9 left panel and a right panel mostly 8 with one 6.
